q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution
Today is 2026-08-15. Q2 FY2027 earnings will typically be released around August-September 2026 (NVIDIA's fiscal quarters run differently from calendar quarters). Based on the pattern shown in the research, Q1 FY2027 was reported on 2026-05-20 for the quarter ended 2026-04-26. Q2 FY2027 likely ends around late July 2026, with earnings expected in late August 2026 — suggesting **approximately 1-2 weeks until resolution**.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

**NVIDIA already provided its Q2 FY2027 guidance on May 20, 2026**: $91.0 billion ± 2%, which translates to a range of **$89.2 billion to $92.8 billion**.

The question asks what guidance will be **in** the Q2 FY2027 earnings release. This guidance has already been communicated. Unless the company issues a substantial revision (rare without major negative developments), the forward guidance announced at that time is what will appear in the formal 8-K/earnings release.

The actual guidance point is $91.0 billion. The range given in the question ($99.5B to $115.5B) suggests expectations for higher-end outcomes, but this appears to be the *possible range* rather than the expected range.

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA reaffirms, slightly adjusts, or provides updated guidance. Given:
- Q1 actual revenue ($81.6B) vs. guidance ($86.84B average estimate) — they beat on growth trajectory
- Q2 guidance already set at $91.0B ± 2%
- No major negative catalysts mentioned in the research
- The $91.0B guidance explicitly excludes China Data Center compute revenue, which could be upside

The median forecast should center near **$91.0 billion**, the already-provided guidance.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Macro deterioration or AI demand slowdown between May and August 2026
- Increased China regulatory headwinds or export restrictions
- Customer inventory corrections or order deferrals
- Supply chain constraints not previously anticipated
- Geopolitical escalation impacting customer spending
- However, with guidance already issued, downward revisions would require material negative developments

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Stronger-than-expected demand for H100/H200 GPUs continuing
- China revenue exceptions or reclassifications allowing more revenue recognition
- Data center customers accelerating orders ahead of next-gen launches
- Mix shift toward higher-margin products
- The guidance already excludes China compute revenue, so any clarity on what *can* be sold there would be upside
- Momentum from Q1 results ($81.6B with 20% QoQ growth) could justify raising guidance

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

**From the research provided:**
- Q1 FY2027 actual: $81.6 billion (May 2026)
- Q2 FY2027 guidance (already issued): $91.0 billion ± 2%, i.e., $89.2B–$92.8B
- Analyst consensus at time of Q1 earnings: $91.8 billion (range $90.3B–$96.7B)

The question frame ($99.5B–$115.5B range) appears calibrated for scenarios where guidance is raised significantly, but this seems higher than the current trajectory suggests. The already-issued $91.0B guidance is the anchoring point.

Historical NVIDIA patterns: The company typically provides relatively confident guidance with ±2% ranges, and often guides to sustainable levels. A jump from $91.0B guidance to mid-$100B+ would represent ~12–25% upside from already-provided guidance.

---

## My reasoning:

The critical fact is that **NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 forward guidance has already been issued** as of May 20, 2026, at **$91.0 billion ± 2%**. The question asks what guidance will be in the earnings release, which typically reaffirms or makes modest adjustments to previously communicated guidance.

Given:
1. Guidance was set just ~3 months prior to the August 2026 earnings release
2. No major negative catalysts documented
3. The range in the question ($99.5B–$115.5B) appears to be the *possible* range, not the expected range
4. Analyst consensus was $91.8B with a range up to $96.7B at the time of Q1 earnings

The most likely outcome is guidance **near $91.0 billion**, potentially with modest upside (to $92–94B range) if momentum continues. The upper bound of the provided range ($115.5B) would require extraordinary acceleration.

My estimate:
- **Low (10th percentile)**: ~$89.0B (guidance misses on downside)
- **Median (50th percentile)**: ~$91.0B (reaffirms existing guidance)
- **High (90th percentile)**: ~$94.5B (raises guidance modestly, capturing upside)

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion for the first quarter ended April 26, 2026, marking an 85% increase from a year ago and a 20% increase from the previous quarter [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This surpassed the average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA's outlook, released on May 20, 2026, projects revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This guidance does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be around 74.9% and 75.0%, respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points, with operating expenses of approximately $8.5 billion (GAAP) and $8.3 billion (non-GAAP) [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). For the full fiscal year 2027, tax rates are anticipated to be between 16.0% and 18.0% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). Analysts' consensus revenue for Q2 2027 is $91.8 billion, with a range of $90.3 billion to $96.7 billion [tickerleague.com](https://tickerleague.com/companies/NVDA/estimates).
